narrative.headline: Spain are the tournament favourites with Rodri confirmed fit and Yamal back from injury. France are the closest challengers, backed by a sustained market premium well above the model. England and Portugal are genuine semi-final contenders, with Argentina the leading South American threat. Netherlands and Japan open shorthanded after confirmed key injuries.

spain.summary: Spain are the favourites, with Rodri fit and Yamal back from injury.
spain.why: Rodri is back at full fitness and Yamal has recovered from injury, so nothing this week weakens Spain. Our ratings put them at 18% and the market at 16%, both clear of the field, and we land at 16%.

france.summary: France are the closest challengers to Spain, the market backing them well above our ratings.
france.why: Our ratings put France near 8% on recent results, but the market has backed them at 16% all month, reading in a big-tournament pedigree the ratings can't measure. We trust the market more here and land at 14%, between the two.

portugal.summary: Portugal are genuine semi-final contenders, a little ahead of our ratings.
portugal.why: Our ratings have Portugal at 8% and the market a little higher at 10%; we lean towards the market and land at 9%. No injuries or selection news touched them this week.

england.summary: England are genuine semi-final contenders, backed by squad depth.
england.why: Our ratings have England at 7% on recent results, the market higher at 11%, reading in the strength and depth of the squad. We trust the market more and land at 10%, just behind the top group.

argentina.summary: Argentina are the strongest South American side, with Martinez fit again in goal.
argentina.why: Emiliano Martinez has recovered from a fractured finger and is cleared to play, lifting Argentina slightly. Our ratings rate them higher than the market, 11% against 8%, and we land at 9% between the two.

brazil.summary: Brazil stay in the leading pack despite an opening-match doubt.
brazil.why: Neymar misses the opening match and Alisson is easing back from injury, but neither changes Brazil's overall chances much. Our ratings and the market almost agree, at 9%, and we land there.

germany.summary: Germany are mid-pack contenders, with Neuer fit again after a calf injury.
germany.why: Neuer has recovered from a calf injury and is training fully again, a small boost. Our ratings have Germany at 7% and the market lower at 5%; we lean towards the market and land at 6%.

netherlands.summary: The Netherlands open shorthanded after two midfielders were ruled out.
netherlands.why: Xavi Simons and Jerdy Schouten are both out for the tournament with knee injuries, which lowers our estimate. Beyond that our ratings and the market agree, leaving the Netherlands at 4%.

japan.summary: Japan open shorthanded after losing two key players.
japan.why: Wataru Endo and Kaoru Mitoma are both out of the squad injured, weakening Japan's midfield and attack. The losses lower their chances a little, though there is enough cover to keep the fall small.

narrative.focus_story: England enter the 2026 World Cup at 10.2% title probability, below the bookmaker consensus of around 11% but above the pure model estimate of 7.1%. The market premium is earned by squad depth and tournament experience: England are among the highest-value squads in the field and Saka's Achilles management looks precarious in fixtures but is not a confirmed absence. The mixture blends model and market evidence at a 25/75 split, placing England as a genuine semi-final threat but not quite on the level of Spain or France. Key risks are the bracket draw and Saka load management decisions in the group stage.

slot_rationales.R32-slot-A: USA host Paraguay at SoFi Stadium in a Group D opener; Pulisic leads the USMNT and home advantage is meaningful at a sold-out California venue, while Paraguay are weakened by the Enciso injury.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-B: Canada drew 1-1 with Bosnia-Herzegovina in their opener, confirming genuine parity; Larin's substitute equaliser suggests Canada can compete but Bosnia remain a threat through set-pieces.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-C: Brazil face Morocco without Neymar and with Morocco carrying defensive injury concerns from the Norway friendly; Vinicius Jr and Raphinha anchor Brazil's attack at 8.1% title probability.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-D: Argentina face Algeria with Messi leading the attack and a fully fit Martinez in goal after his fractured finger cleared on June 12; Argentina are the leading South American contender at 8.5%.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-E: South Korea beat Czech Republic 2-1 in their opener, an early confidence boost; Czech Republic's Schick remains the group's sharpest finisher and a genuine threat across remaining group fixtures.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-F: Mexico face South Africa in Group F; Mexico sit at 0.7% title probability and are rated below their historical market standing against a competitive African opponent.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-G: France at 14.4% lead their group with Mbappe and Griezmann; the mixture grants substantial weight to the market's sustained 16% consensus while retaining some model scepticism about qualifying group difficulty.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-H: Spain at 17.1% are the clear tournament favourite; Rodri brings confirmed full fitness in midfield and Yamal returns as a substitute-impact player for the opener against Cabo Verde.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-I: England at 10.2% face their group opener with Saka under Achilles load management; the market's 11% consensus is closely matched after blending the model estimate with market evidence at a 25/75 split.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-J: Netherlands are at 4.2% after confirmed ACL losses for Xavi Simons and Jerdy Schouten; De Jong, Gravenberch and Reijnders absorb the midfield load against Japan in the group opener.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-K: Portugal at 9.7% bring Ronaldo and Bruno Fernandes into a group they are expected to lead; a consistent knockout-round threat rated above England per the model's squad quality assessment.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-L: Colombia at 2.2% sit well below their Copa America 2024 finalist credit; both bookmakers and Polymarket agree in discounting Colombia, and the mixture reflects the market consensus over the higher model estimate.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-M: Germany at 5.8% are a balanced European contender with Musiala and Wirtz in the attack; Neuer's confirmed fitness removes a goalkeeper uncertainty that had briefly clouded the outlook.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-N: Belgium at 2.7% are rated below the model estimate of 4.4%; the market discount is consistent across both bookmaker and prediction-market legs, and the mixture gives significant weight to that consensus.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-O: Uruguay at 2.1% are rated above their market price; Nunez and Valverde provide genuine knockout-round potential per the model's squad-quality assessment and strong qualifying record.
slot_rationales.R32-slot-P: Croatia at 1.7% are the darkest of the dark horses; Modric's tournament experience gives them a knockout ceiling well above their outright price if the bracket opens favourably.

narrative.travel_memo: The tournament opens across North American venues with Spain confirmed as favourites after Rodri's full fitness clearance. Netherlands and Japan both begin their campaigns significantly weakened by injury: Simons and Schouten are out with ACL damage for the Dutch, while Japan lose Endo and Mitoma from their squad. France carry a strong market premium above the model estimate, reflecting confident market pricing sustained throughout qualifying. Brazil face Morocco without Neymar in their Group C opener. Argentina go in with Martinez passed fit after his fractured finger recovery. Watch England's Saka load management and the Colombia overrating risk as group-stage results accumulate.

quant_findings.summary: Six confirmed news items priced via perturbation_impact (noise floor 0.59pp throughout). Four are material signal; two are moot or sub-floor. Seven model-vs-market base disagreements exceed noise floor, with France (+7.7pp) and England (+3.9pp) the largest structural gaps; Colombia and Belgium carry
findings: NOISE FLOOR: 0.59pp (paired-seed, all perturbation_impact calls). All deltas below are from executed simulations.

NETHERLANDS (Simons + Schouten ACL, led-0002): strength delta -0.10 -> title delta -2.47pp (4.2x floor). Squad_players confirms both players already excluded from registered squad; model may partially embed via squad-value covariate (~14% of hypothetical full squad value gone). This is an UPPER BOUN

JAPAN (Endo + Mitoma both out, led-0001/0006): strength delta -0.10 -> title delta -0.77pp (1.3x floor; marginal signal). Squad_players confirms both absent from registered squad. Endo (DM/captain) + Mitoma (key winger) represent ~15.6% of hypothetical full squad value. Japan Polymarket (2.08%) has

GERMANY (Neuer confirmed fit, led-0003/0012/0013): strength delta +0.04 -> title delta +1.89pp (3.2x floor). Resolves slight calf-doubt scenario. Paradoxically widens model-vs-market gap since market already had Germany discounted (-0.053 in market base). Post-news model Germany ~8.3% vs market 5.22

ARGENTINA (Martinez fit, led-0008/0009): strength delta +0.02 -> title delta +0.90pp (1.5x floor). Fractured finger resolved; Martinez completed full training with both gloves 2026-06-12. Small positive confirmation.

WORLD 2 - market_base (weight 0.55): 8-team market inversion via wq.implied_delta -- France +0.150, England +0.0895, Portugal +0.0311, Spain -0.035, Argentina -0.0548, Germany -0.0428, Belgium -0.1112, Colombia -0.1718. agent.change_justification: Steelman and evidence per escalating move, all computed in mixture-003 (quant-002): France +6.33pp -- steelman: Mbappe at peak tournament form and France's 2018/2022 final appearances reflect quality the qualifying goal-rate model cannot capture; market has maintained 16% consistently; counter-case granted at 75% market weight, yielding 14.4% (still below market's 16%). England +3.06pp -- steelman: Bellingham settled, squad the most valuable in the field, market correct at 11%; mixture at 10.2% grants the steelman case by weighting market worlds at 75%, computation in market_base and market_evidence worlds. Colombia -2.74pp -- steelman: model is right that Copa America 2024 final and WCQ wins over Argentina reflect genuine quality; counter: both bookmaker and Polymarket legs agree on 1.56% de-vigged, and copa-form does not predict World Cup winners; market inversion delta -0.1718 applied in market_base and market_evidence worlds (75% combined weight), computed in mixture-003. Belgium -1.74pp -- steelman: De Bruyne and Lukaku squad quality above 2.3% market; counter: consistent market discount across both legs reflects forward-looking view of ageing squad and De Bruyne injury history; market inversion -0.1112 applied at 75% weight in mixture-003. Japan -0.36pp -- news-driven: Endo (led-0001) and Mitoma (led-0006) confirmed out, delta mean=-0.06 each in model_evidence and market_evidence worlds; steelman that Japan's squad depth absorbs this is plausible but the evidence is hard confirmed, computed in mixture-003. Mexico -0.20pp -- model rates Mexico below market on squad value; no market inversion applied (below inversion threshold); steelman that home-continent passion lifts Mexico is unquantifiable and not backed by a confirmed ledger entry; model_base drives the estimate in mixture-003.
